title: Request Diagnostic Compass — Correlation Grid & Temporal Lens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact investigative workspace for the Console that surfaces correlated requests, spans and timing relationships in two coordinated views: a Correlation Grid (compact matrix of related requests and metadata) and a Temporal Lens (detail timeline with scrubber + span grouping). Goal: reduce mean time-to-diagnose for customer ops and platform engineers by making cross-service correlation and temporal anomalies discoverable without leaving the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation Grid shows up to 50 correlated requests for a selected root request, sortable by latency, cost tokens, and failure rate
Temporal Lens synchronizes detail timeline when a grid row is selected; scrubber supports jump-to-span and play/pause replay
Filters: time window, correlation-id, service, status code, token-count; combinations persist in URL
Prototype includes accessible keyboard navigation for span focus and a condensed compact mode for small screens
Engineer handoff includes component tokens, responsive behavior, and a performance budget for timeline rendering (target: 60fps for 200 spans)
Design validated by at least 5 internal engineers and 3 customer support scenarios with qualitative success criteria (faster root cause identification)
All snippets and external links included in ticket (Figma, PRD, GitHub draft issue, demo video)
design_notes: Correlation Grid is intentionally compact: each row is a condensed summary (service, endpoint, duration, cost tokens, error badge); hover expands contextual tags
Trade-off: showing full span stacks in the grid makes scanning harder; we push full span detail into the Temporal Lens to keep the grid scannable

We measured two layout directions: side-by-side grid+timeline vs stacked panel. Side-by-side works for widescreen consoles and keeps temporal context visible during scanning; stacked is preserved for narrow widths
Performance consideration: virtualized row rendering and incremental span hydration; timeline should lazy-load span bodies when a row is focused
Correlation heuristics: first-class correlation-id, fallbacks by parent_span_id and matching trace_id across services
Cost integration: add a per-request token column (rounded) and allow quick jump to Cost Breakdown for that request in Console (link-out)
Accessibility: color palette keeps error badges to a single accent color with shape alternatives; keyboard shortcuts: G to focus grid, L to focus lens, P to pin request
decisions: Use correlation-id as primary grouping key; include heuristic matches where correlation-id absent
Default sort: latency desc (with sticky user preference saved per user)
Timeline shows aggregated span lanes with an expand/collapse affordance rather than always showing full stack
Persist filters in URL to allow sharing deep-links to investigative states
Prototype will ship without live streaming first (static capture + play) to limit scope; streaming to be scoped as follow-up
